limitations: No formal millimetre calibration, tested loaded travel envelope, or independent target-point acceptance.
Each group samples only baseline plus one single-sided perturbation of each axis and two returns; this is three unique command points, not a 2D coverage dataset.
Right-hand returns retain roughly 3-4 image pixels horizontally; image hysteresis does not identify its electrical or mechanical cause.
NCC tracks deformable image patches; ROI choice, projection, blur, lighting and linkage motion can bias the result.
Other groups are not held by PWM during each pair test; simultaneous full-puppet behavior remains unverified.
Selected steady top images do not exclude transient collisions, subtle slipping or occluded interference.
Output OFF confirms PWM controller state, not servo power isolation, shaft angle or load holding.
All tiger initial and pair samples are quarantined after the user report; numerical observations are retained only as diagnostic evidence, not accepted calibration or replay data.
Old command registers and visual estimates do not establish a reliable physical starting position. Re-enabling a matching register value can still result in motion.
No exact physical tension onset, slipping tie, or specific mechanical failure is inferred from this record.
The aborted all-axis attempt has no sample_begin and did not establish four-axis holding; finally OFF does not prove there was no movement before shutdown.
next_work: Keep all real motion disabled and do not replay or adopt these old pulse values.
Perform mechanical inspection with servo power isolated before considering further live work.
Establish a reliably known physical starting position and verify any software fixes offline before a separately reviewed restart.
Reassess tracking, coupled geometry and camera coverage before collecting a new accepted calibration dataset; retain the current records only for diagnosis.
